---
title: "macOS launchd and alerts"
subtitle: "The weekday job, the wrapper script, failure alerts and the heartbeat."
---

A user LaunchAgent runs `gh-inbox` every weekday morning through a small wrapper script. If the Mac is asleep at that time, launchd runs the job when it wakes. On failure the wrapper raises a persistent alert, one that stays on screen until you dismiss it, not a banner that slides away. A shell alias runs the same thing by hand.

## What to check

### The installed command

- [ ] `gh-inbox` is installed with `uv tool install` (or `pipx install`) and lives at {{< meta facts.path.bin >}}. launchd calls it by that full path, never by bare name.
- [ ] `which gh` gives a directory that's in the job's `PATH` below (`/opt/homebrew/bin` on Apple silicon).

### The wrapper script

{{< meta facts.path.wrapper >}}, executable (`chmod +x`):

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Run gh-inbox; on failure, raise a persistent alert naming the log.
LOG={{< meta facts.path.log >}}
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG")"
{
  echo "--- $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
  {{< meta facts.path.bin >}}
} >>"$LOG" 2>&1
status=$?
if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
  /usr/bin/osascript -e "display alert \"gh-inbox failed (exit $status)\" message \"See $LOG\" as critical"
fi
exit "$status"
```

- [ ] `display alert` (not `display notification`) is what makes the alert persistent.
- [ ] An alert can come with an inbox that was still written: if only one source failed, the block shows a warning line naming it, and the log says why.

### The LaunchAgent

{{< meta facts.path.plist >}}:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
  <key>Label</key>
  <string>{{< meta facts.launchd.label >}}</string>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  <array>
    <string>/bin/zsh</string>
    <string>-c</string>
    <string>{{< meta facts.path.wrapper >}}</string>
  </array>
  <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
  <dict>
    <key>PATH</key>
    <string>/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin</string>
  </dict>
  <!-- Weekdays 1 (Monday) to 5 (Friday) at {{< meta facts.time.job >}} -->
  <key>StartCalendarInterval</key>
  <array>
    <dict><key>Weekday</key><integer>1</integer><key>Hour</key><integer>{{< meta facts.time.job_hour >}}</integer><key>Minute</key><integer>{{< meta facts.time.job_minute >}}</integer></dict>
    <dict><key>Weekday</key><integer>2</integer><key>Hour</key><integer>{{< meta facts.time.job_hour >}}</integer><key>Minute</key><integer>{{< meta facts.time.job_minute >}}</integer></dict>
    <dict><key>Weekday</key><integer>3</integer><key>Hour</key><integer>{{< meta facts.time.job_hour >}}</integer><key>Minute</key><integer>{{< meta facts.time.job_minute >}}</integer></dict>
    <dict><key>Weekday</key><integer>4</integer><key>Hour</key><integer>{{< meta facts.time.job_hour >}}</integer><key>Minute</key><integer>{{< meta facts.time.job_minute >}}</integer></dict>
    <dict><key>Weekday</key><integer>5</integer><key>Hour</key><integer>{{< meta facts.time.job_hour >}}</integer><key>Minute</key><integer>{{< meta facts.time.job_minute >}}</integer></dict>
  </array>
</dict>
</plist>
```

- [ ] `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/{{< meta facts.launchd.label >}}` shows the job loaded. After editing the plist, reload it:

  ```bash
  launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u) {{< meta facts.path.plist >}}
  launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) {{< meta facts.path.plist >}}
  ```

- [ ] `launchctl kickstart gui/$(id -u)/{{< meta facts.launchd.label >}}` runs it now; the daily note's stamp updates.
- [ ] The job goes through `/bin/zsh -c` so the `~` in the wrapper path expands; launchd itself doesn't expand `~`. The wrapper does its own logging, so the plist needs no `StandardOutPath`.
- [ ] The time is {{< meta facts.time.job >}}, before the triage reminder at {{< meta facts.time.triage >}}. Calendar-interval jobs missed while the Mac sleeps run on wake; jobs missed while it's shut down don't.

### The alias

In `~/.zshrc`:

```bash
alias {{< meta facts.launchd.alias >}}='{{< meta facts.path.wrapper >}}'
```

- [ ] {{< meta facts.launchd.alias >}} refreshes the inbox through the same wrapper, so a manual failure alerts and logs the same way.

### Failure visibility

- [ ] The log at {{< meta facts.path.log >}} has one `---` stamped section per run.
- [ ] The heartbeat is the `updated at` stamp in today's inbox block. If it's missing or not from today, the job didn't run, even if no alert appeared (for example, the Mac was off).

## How it lines up with the other tools

{{< include _partials/schedule.qmd >}}

| Here | Must line up with |
|---|---|
| The command `gh-inbox` | Reads {{< meta facts.path.config >}} ([config file](config.qmd)) |
| `PATH` in the plist | Where `gh` is installed and authenticated ([GitHub settings](github-settings.qmd)) |
| Job time {{< meta facts.time.job >}} | Before the reminder and calendar block ([Reminders and Calendar](reminders-calendar.qmd)) |
| The job succeeding | Today's daily note existing at {{< meta facts.vault.daily_folder >}} ([Obsidian](obsidian.qmd)) |
